## Background

Nightly main-to-dev sync. N=29: all of `dev..main` at selection, oldest first.
- Dev base: `ff20ed54650dd47ba21989767dfc0068d8c6f73e`
- Slice tip: `364eef70a30aacdc622e75f6f437b50c2ef18278`

Imported: 7d3f0fb3 4422adc5 18bc49d2 9314b010 0a2f6eec 01e36a2a 9ef1a71d 20527695 ea99fdfc ed9c2c8c 70527409 f9d606dc 22f272e0 886b253d 5eb70478 e3f52838 1142209a 19895daf 63f687dc 3ddfe0fe 9dd63d99 29319fd9 fdbd9f95 2abdd0d1 17fc7ba1 3ca52d95 f368e946 259f6a7c 364eef70

## What changed

31 commits (N+2): the 29 main commits unchanged, merge `7e6f051b` (parents dev `ff20ed54`, main `364eef70`) and repair `8ba4544f`.
- 40 files conflicted. 27 of them reuse the resolution reviewed in #8510 (same 3-way inputs). The merge message lists the rest.
- Kept from dev: pyproject.toml, uv.lock, Dockerfile.ci.dev, CODEOWNERS and the DSA FLOPs accounting.
- Repair: restores 2 dev-only hooks in `data_samplers.py` (#5771, #4751) and adapts 3 dev tests to main's DCP V2 API. It also fixes review 5685135943: hybrid mock SFT data in `pretrain_hybrid.py` and KPool FLOPs in `training.py`.

## Details

- Pre-push advisory: 1636 possible dev-only removals in 81 files, each traced to a slice commit or to the repair's test updates. No CODEOWNERS or dependency findings.
- Remerge-diff of `7e6f051b` reviewed per file.
- Labels needed: `Run functional tests`, `Run MBridge tests`, `determinism-exempt`.

## Tested

Local H100, image `megatron-lm@sha256:c45d8f4e1b811b4e83dd8d80c5953dc1f9952c4fee5b83776851c5a5243e4e80`. 145/145 rows passed. No CI results were reused and no upstream skips were used.
- Unit 61/61: `data/**` (807 passed) and `unit_tests/**` (4319 passed) on `8ba4544f`. The other 59 rows are kept from earlier heads because their inputs did not change.
- Functional 84/84: 83 on `7e6f051b` and `gpt3_mcore_te_tp2_pp1_cp4_dcp` on `16a1f289`. Later repairs do not change their inputs.

GitHub CI on `8ba4544f`: CICD Megatron-LM run 40728412120 passed (203 jobs passed, 9 skipped, including the MBridge and NeMo-RL jobs). `Nemo_CICD_Test`, Installation Test, Megatron-Core build, Copyright and Process group also passed. The DCO gate fails on 10 imported main commits and needs a maintainer override.

This pull request requires additional validation before any workflows can run on NVIDIA's runners.

Pull request vetters can view their responsibilities [here](https://docs.gha-runners.nvidia.com/cpr/vetters).

Contributors can view more details about this message [here](https://docs.gha-runners.nvidia.com/cpr/contributors).

Requesting changes on `16a1f289` for two omissions in the main-to-dev integration:

1. **Restore Hybrid mock SFT.** [`pretrain_hybrid.py:505`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/16a1f289dedb71b2532782a78d198eb51fcacbdc/pretrain_hybrid.py#L505) always selects `SFTDataset` under `--sft`, dropping dev's `MockSFTDataset` branch. With `--sft --mock-data`, the mock builder passes `dataset_path=None` to the real JSON loader. Please restore the conditional selection and cover this flag combination in the Hybrid provider.

2. **Keep main's KPool FLOPs fix while preserving dev's MTP numbering.** The [production counter](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/16a1f289dedb71b2532782a78d198eb51fcacbdc/megatron/training/training.py#L2380) never reads `dsa_indexer_kpool`. With no MTP and zero indexer loss, the in-tree DSA fixture returns 46,736,605,184 for both pool sizes 1 and 4; main's pool-4 result is 46,772,733,625, matching the independent pooling oracle. The numbering difference does not explain this no-MTP case. Please integrate the pooling terms from #7043 and restore public-counter coverage. This is an omitted reporting fix, not a measured training-performance regression.

The caller-owned CP, replay-copy, static-wrapper and SBHD frontend repairs are present; we are not repeating the old #8510 requests for those fixes. These findings use source review and isolated provider/arithmetic probes, not GPU training validation.

CI attempt 2 of run `40705424337` is still in progress on this head: linting now passes and the GB200 container build is still running, so there are no unit or functional results yet, and the MBridge job was skipped. This incomplete coverage is separate from the two change requests above.

Re-reviewed `8ba4544f`: both change requests in my previous review are addressed. Hybrid mock-SFT selection is restored, and the standard DSA counter now includes the KPool terms while preserving dev's MTP numbering. The added tests and isolated provider/arithmetic checks support those fixes; I found no new confirmed code blocker in this delta.

I am waiting for critical validation on this head before approving. Run `40728412120` is currently waiting, without completed unit/functional results. The updated local-test claims are noted, but I haven't verified their logs or the equivalence of reused earlier-head results. This is a validation wait, not another request to fix F1/F2.

Approving `8ba4544f`. Both requests from my earlier review are fixed: Hybrid mock-SFT selection is restored, and KPool FLOPs are integrated while preserving dev's MTP numbering.

[CI run 40728412120](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/actions/runs/40728412120) passed on the reviewed tree: 203 jobs succeeded and 9 were skipped. Its merge-preview tree is identical to this head. The 12 provider cases and 36 KPool public-counter cases actually ran and passed, along with the relevant CP/packing regressions, THD tests and GB200 DSv4 graph replays.

Coverage limits: MBridge was not selected, so external Bridge compatibility is not qualified by this run. The DCP and packed train/eval functional cases provide lightweight smoke/resume coverage, not golden-loss or exhaustive graph validation.

+# Copyright (c) 2026 NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved.
+
+"""Select all unit-test buckets on one CPU runner and publish the GPU matrix."""
+
+import hashlib
+import json
+import logging
+import os
+import shutil
+import subprocess
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+
+def _actions(operation: str, *args: str) -> None:
+    # The workflow supplies the small adapter for GitHub's Node-only SDKs.
+    subprocess.run(
+        [os.environ["TESTMON_NODE"], "-e", os.environ["TESTMON_ACTIONS"], operation, *args],
+        check=True,
+    )
+
+
+def _python(script: str, args: list[str]) -> dict[str, str]:
+    output = subprocess.check_output(
+        [sys.executable, f"tests/unit_tests/{script}", *args], text=True
+    )
+    logger.info(output.strip())
+    return dict(line.split("=", 1) for line in output.strip().splitlines())
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    """Restore each baseline, run the existing selector, and upload its plan."""
+    if os.environ["TARGET_BRANCH"] != "main":
+        raise ValueError("Testmon selection requires main")
+    platform = os.environ["RECIPE_PLATFORM"]
+    generation = f"{os.environ['GITHUB_RUN_ID']}-{os.environ['GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT']}"
+    temporary = Path(os.environ["RUNNER_TEMP"])
+    cache_dir = Path("assets_dir/testmon")
+    plan = "assets_dir/testmon-plan/plan.json"
+    matrix = []
+    summary = [
+        "### Unit tests selection",
+        "",
+        "| Bucket | Mode | GPU required |",
+        "| --- | --- | --- |",
+    ]
+
+    # Restore sequentially: the path is part of the existing cache version.
+    for entry in json.loads(os.environ["BUCKETS"]):
+        bucket = entry["bucket"]
+        logger.info("Selecting %s", bucket)
+        identity = _python(
+            "testmon_cache.py",
+            [
+                "identity",
+                "--bucket",
+                bucket,
+                "--platform",
+                platform,
+                "--output",
+                str(temporary / "unit-testmon-identity.json"),
+            ],
+        )
+        if cache_dir.exists():
+            shutil.rmtree(cache_dir)
+        matched_key = ""
+        key_file = temporary / "unit-testmon-matched-key"
+        prefix = identity["cache_prefix"]
+        try:
+            _actions(
+                "restore", str(cache_dir), f"{prefix}lookup-{generation}", prefix, str(key_file)
+            )
+            matched_key = key_file.read_text()
+        except subprocess.CalledProcessError:
+            logger.warning("Testmon cache restore failed for %s", bucket)
+        result = _python(
+            "testmon_selector.py",
+            [
+                "select",
+                "--cache-dir",
+                str(cache_dir),
+                "--bucket",
+                bucket,
+                "--platform",
+                platform,
+                "--source-sha",
+                os.environ["SOURCE_SHA"],
+                "--matched-key",
+                matched_key,
+                "--pr-files-dir",
+                os.environ["PR_FILES_DIR"],
+                "--output",
+                plan,
+            ],
+        )
+        mode, has_tests = result["mode"], result["has_tests"]
+        if (
+            mode not in {"selected", "full"}
+            or has_tests not in {"true", "false"}
+            or (mode == "full" and has_tests != "true")
+        ):
+            raise ValueError(f"Invalid Testmon selection result for {bucket}")
+        artifact = ""
+        if mode == "selected":
+            bucket_hash = hashlib.sha256(bucket.encode()).hexdigest()[:16]
+            artifact = f"unit-test-plan-{platform}-{bucket_hash}-{generation}"
+            # Upload empty plans too: the coverage gate uses them as skip evidence.
+            _actions("upload", artifact, plan, "assets_dir/testmon-plan")
+        if has_tests == "true":
+            matrix.append(
+                {
+                    **entry,
+                    "mode": "preselected" if mode == "selected" else "full",
+                    "plan_artifact": artifact,
+                }
+            )
+        summary.append(f"| `{bucket}` | {mode} | {has_tests} |")
+
+    with Path(os.environ["GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"]).open("a") as stream:
+        stream.write("\n".join(summary) + "\n")
+    with Path(os.environ["GITHUB_OUTPUT"]).open("a") as stream:
+        stream.write(f"matrix={json.dumps(matrix, separators=(',', ':'))}\n")
+        stream.write(f"has_tests={str(bool(matrix)).lower()}\n")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(message)s")
+    main()

+"""Compatibility adapters for the deprecated Hybrid-CP batch-helper keywords."""
+
+import inspect
+import warnings
+from functools import wraps
+from typing import Callable, ParamSpec, TypeVar
+
+_Parameters = ParamSpec("_Parameters")
+_Result = TypeVar("_Result")
+_DEPRECATED_KEYWORDS = (
+    ("is_hybrid_cp", "dynamic_cp"),
+    ("hybrid_cp_group_func", "dynamic_cp_group_func"),
+)
+
+
+def deprecated_hybrid_cp_kwargs(
+    function: Callable[_Parameters, _Result],
+) -> Callable[_Parameters, _Result]:
+    """Accept old keyword names without changing positional arguments or new signatures."""
+
+    @wraps(function)
+    def wrapped(*args: _Parameters.args, **kwargs: _Parameters.kwargs) -> _Result:
+        for old_name, new_name in _DEPRECATED_KEYWORDS:
+            if old_name in kwargs:
+                if new_name in kwargs:
+                    raise TypeError(f"Cannot pass both {old_name} and {new_name}")
+                warnings.warn(
+                    f"{old_name} is deprecated; use {new_name} instead.",
+                    DeprecationWarning,
+                    stacklevel=2,
+                )
+                kwargs[new_name] = kwargs.pop(old_name)
+        return function(*args, **kwargs)
+
+    # MBridge detects THD CP support by inspecting the deprecated flag's name.
+    # Keep keyword aliases discoverable, not just accepted at call time.
+    signature = inspect.signature(function)
+    aliases = [
+        inspect.Parameter(
+            old_name,
+            inspect.Parameter.KEYWORD_ONLY,
+            default=None,
+            annotation=signature.parameters[new_name].annotation,
+        )
+        for old_name, new_name in _DEPRECATED_KEYWORDS
+        if new_name in signature.parameters
+    ]
+    wrapped.__signature__ = signature.replace(parameters=[*signature.parameters.values(), *aliases])
+    return wrapped

+"""Pure topology helpers shared by dynamic CP initialization and scheduling."""
+
+from typing import List
+
+
+def get_valid_dynamic_context_parallel_group_sizes(total_size: int) -> List[int]:
+    """Return runtime CP sizes that can partition a DPxCP rank list exactly.
+
+    Power-of-two subgroups are used when they evenly divide the rank list. The
+    full DPxCP group is always valid and reuses the existing communicator.
+    """
+    if total_size < 1:
+        raise ValueError(f"Dynamic CP group size must be positive, got {total_size}")
+
+    group_sizes = []
+    group_size = 1
+    while group_size < total_size:
+        if total_size % group_size == 0:
+            group_sizes.append(group_size)
+        group_size *= 2
+    group_sizes.append(total_size)
+    return group_sizes

 # Data Pipeline
 
+Packed training and evaluation support `--pad-packed-seq-alignment N` (a CP-local
+token multiple before SP) or `max` (pad to `--max-seqlen-per-dp-cp-rank`). MXFP8
+automatically requires a multiple of 32 tokens after SP; the effective alignment
+combines that requirement with the requested multiple. Padding is added before
+CP layout construction, with masked dummy sequences and consistent THD metadata.
+The scheduler reserves an aligned capacity; padding never truncates valid tokens.
+This eager path does not require CUDA graphs.
+
+When unpacking SFT data, prompt-only sub-sequences are retained so packing can
+still fill all DP ranks; their zero loss masks exclude them from the loss. A DP
+rank can contribute no samples and still receive scheduled work. A global batch
+with no sequences is rejected on all ranks.
+
+Dynamic CP does not currently support `--deterministic-mode`, CUDA graphs, or
+router z-loss. Configuration validation rejects these combinations before training.
+Static sequence packing without dynamic CP retains its existing deterministic-mode
+support. Dynamic CP for Hybrid models follows in PR #7048.
+
+Batch helpers use `dynamic_cp` and `dynamic_cp_group_func`. The old `is_hybrid_cp`
+and `hybrid_cp_group_func` keyword arguments remain accepted with a deprecation
+warning for downstream callers. Positional arguments and the legacy
+`hybrid_cp_group` batch metadata are unchanged during this compatibility window.
+The deprecated keywords also remain visible to signature-based feature detection
+used by downstream consumers such as MBridge.
+
+The `gpt_packed_train_eval` functional test runs the real GPT entrypoint on eight
+GPUs with TP2/PP2, synthetic variable-length data, and static or dynamic packing.
+It checks finite training/evaluation losses and gradient norms, a completed
+checkpoint, and CP1/CP2 coverage in both training and evaluation. It does not
+claim deterministic or golden-loss equivalence. Run it from the repository root:
+
+```bash
+python tests/functional_tests/test_cases/gpt/gpt_packed_train_eval/run_test.py \
+  --packing-mode dynamic --output-path /path/to/a/new/output-directory
+```

+# Muon with MFSDP v2
+
+## Background
+
+MFSDP shards one **module** at a time. By default, parameters owned by that
+module with the same dtype and `requires_grad` form one parameter group.
+Each group packs its weights and gradients into separate contiguous
+buffers. Ranks store local segments of these buffers. Weights are
+all-gathered for module computation; gradients are reduce-scattered after
+backward.
+
+The [sharding placements](../megatron_fsdp/experimental/placement.py)
+determine how the buffers are partitioned:
+
+- `RowAtomic`: keeps rows intact, with equal-sized rank segments. This is
+  the default for ordinary floating-point parameters.
+- `BlockAtomic(k)`: keeps blocks of `k` consecutive rows intact, with
+  equal-sized rank segments. Keeping each quantization block on one rank
+  simplifies blockwise quantization. MXFP8 uses `k=32`.
+- `TensorAtomic`: assigns each complete parameter to one rank. Rank
+  segments may differ in size or be empty. Keeping weights, gradients,
+  and momentum on the same owner makes Muon's optimizer step
+  communication-free.
+
+By contrast,
+[PyTorch FSDP2](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.14/distributed.fsdp.fully_shard.html#communication-grouping-and-scheduling)
+shards **each parameter independently along dim 0**. Both systems
+can group parameters for communication; the difference is how they form
+the shards.
+
+### Example
+
+Five trainable FP32 parameters owned by one module are packed as follows.
+This RowAtomic layout comes from
+[`test_compute_layout_fills_lcm_padding_gaps`](../../../../../../tests/unit_tests/distributed/mfsdp_v2/test_dbuffer.py#L60)
+and the illustration in
+[`build_for_row_atomic`](../megatron_fsdp/experimental/layout_builder.py#L39).
+
+```text
+Shapes: P0=(2,6), P1=(4,4), P2=(4,4), P3=(1,2), P4=(1,6)
+One group buffer, 12 elements per rank (including padding)
+
+rank 0 [ 0,12): | P0 row 0              | P0 row 1               |
+rank 1 [12,24): | P1 row 0      | P1 row 1      | P1 row 2       |
+rank 2 [24,36): | P1 row 3      | P3    | gap   | P2 row 0       |
+rank 3 [36,48): | P2 row 1      | P2 row 2      | P2 row 3       |
+rank 4 [48,60): | P4                    | pad                    |
+```
+
+All-gather assembles these segments into a full group buffer on every
+rank. Gradient reduce-scatter reduces the full buffers and returns the
+corresponding segment to each rank. Afterward, `P0`, `P3`, and `P4` are
+already whole on one rank. Only `P1` and `P2` need reconstruction for local
+full-matrix Muon orthogonalization.
+
+## Challenge
+
+**RowAtomic and BlockAtomic.** Muon orthogonalizes the momentum-derived
+input for each complete logical matrix using Newton–Schulz. Applying it
+independently to row or block shards, or to the concatenated group buffer,
+would change the update. The challenge is to provide whole-matrix inputs
+to Muon while retaining module-level sharding.
+
+**TensorAtomic.** Whole-matrix inputs are already local. The challenge is
+to enforce the layout requested by Muon without substantially slowing
+forward/backward. Block-atomic sharding can distribute parameters unevenly
+while keeping the total data per rank largely balanced. Assigning whole
+matrices can make that distribution unbalanced. If gathering weights or
+reducing gradients takes longer, that extra time could cancel out the time
+saved in the optimizer step.
+
+## Algorithm options
+
+Both options need a separate optimizer for excluded parameters, such as
+biases and embeddings.
+
+### Gather and scatter
+
+**Implemented in [`FsdpMuon`](../megatron_fsdp/experimental/muon.py).** Keep
+weights, gradients, and momentum in the existing sharded layout. For each
+parameter group, after gradient reduction:
+
+1. Update local momentum and construct the orthogonalization inputs.
+2. Gather each split matrix's input to one compute owner.
+3. Run full-matrix Newton–Schulz once on that owner.
+4. Scatter update slices back, apply them to local weight shards, and
+   refresh model weights.
+
+The [owner planner](../megatron_fsdp/experimental/owner_planning.py)
+balances estimated compute across groups, choosing owners from ranks that
+already hold a fragment. [P2P gather/scatter](../megatron_fsdp/experimental/gather_scatter.py)
+moves only remote fragments. In the example, `P0`, `P3`, and `P4` require
+no optimizer-step network traffic. Persistent ownership stays unchanged;
+full inputs and updates exist temporarily on compute owners.
+
+A simpler alternative in [issue #5533](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/issues/5533)
+all-gathers boundary-matrix inputs and duplicates orthogonalization. The
+current path avoids that redundant computation.
+
+### TensorAtomic placement
+
+**Alternative based on [MatrixFSDP](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.05895), tracked
+in [issue #6161](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/issues/6161).** Assign
+each whole matrix, its gradient, and its momentum to one persistent owner;
+other ranks hold empty shards for that matrix.
+
+Using the same five tensors as the background example, one possible owner
+assignment is:
+
+```text
+One group buffer, 52 elements total, no padding
+
+rank 0 [ 0,12): | P0 row 0              | P0 row 1               |
+rank 1 [12,28): | P1 row 0      | P1 row 1      | P1 row 2      | P1 row 3       |
+rank 2 [28,28): empty
+rank 3 [28,44): | P2 row 0      | P2 row 1      | P2 row 2      | P2 row 3       |
+rank 4 [44,52): | P3    | P4                    |
+```
+
+Every matrix is whole on its owner. Rank 2 owns no tensors in this group.
+
+1. Materialize the module's weights from owners for forward/backward.
+2. Reduce each matrix's gradient to its owner.
+3. Update momentum, orthogonalize, and update weights locally on the owner.
+
+This removes optimizer-step matrix communication. Forward/backward should
+[communicate uneven owner segments without padding](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/issues/6161#issuecomment-5229334204).
+MFSDP already provides the [layouts](../megatron_fsdp/experimental/placement.py)
+and [collectives](../megatron_fsdp/experimental/dbuffer.py) for this.
+
+## Tradeoffs
+
+- **Gather/scatter favors forward/backward** through more balanced sharding.
+- **TensorAtomic favors the optimizer** by avoiding
+  gather/scatter communication and temporary buffers.
+
+## Next step
+
+1. **Integrate `FsdpMuon` with `MegatronOptimizer`**, including chaining
+   with an optimizer for excluded parameters.
+2. **Optimize performance.** Overlap communication with Muon computation
+   and make parameter placement aware of hardware topology to keep traffic
+   on fast links, as discussed in [#6368](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/issues/6368).
+3. **Evaluate TensorAtomic at larger scale.** Compare it with gather/scatter
+   on larger models across multiple nodes, measuring forward/backward time,
+   full-step time, and peak memory.

+"""FlashInfer routed-MoE support for per-token NVFP4 x NVFP4 squared-ReLU and SwiGLU experts.
+
+Expert weights are quantized from MCore's BF16 expert stacks with one FP32
+global scale per expert. Activations are quantized online with one FP32 scale
+per token, so no calibration or static input scale is required. The experts
+run on FlashInfer's CuTe DSL block-scaled grouped GEMMs.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+
+import torch
+import torch.nn.functional as F
+
+from megatron.core.inference.moe.flashinfer_mxfp8 import select_routed_mxfp8_active_rows
+from megatron.core.transformer.custom_layers.batch_invariant_kernels import (
+    is_batch_invariant_mode_enabled,
+)
+
+try:
+    import flashinfer
+    from flashinfer import ActivationType, SfLayout, nvfp4_quantize
+    from packaging.version import Version
+
+    # Per-token NVFP4 Relu2 MoE landed in FlashInfer 0.7.0 (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3645).
+    if Version(flashinfer.__version__).release < (0, 7, 0):
+        raise ImportError(
+            f"FlashInfer {flashinfer.__version__} lacks the per-token NVFP4 Relu2 MoE kernels"
+        )
+    from flashinfer import CuteDslMoEWrapper
+    from flashinfer.cute_dsl.utils import convert_sf_to_mma_layout
+
+    _FLASHINFER_NVFP4_IMPORT_ERROR: ImportError | None = None
+except ImportError as exc:
+    _FLASHINFER_NVFP4_IMPORT_ERROR = exc
+
+HAVE_FLASHINFER_ROUTED_NVFP4 = _FLASHINFER_NVFP4_IMPORT_ERROR is None
+
+NVFP4_BLOCK_SIZE = 16
+FLOAT4_E2M1_MAX = 6.0
+FLOAT8_E4M3_MAX = 448.0
+# Per-token quantization folds the row amax into the per-token scale, so the base
+# global scale is the recipe constant 1 / (E4M3_MAX * E2M1_MAX). FlashInfer rejects
+# other values. It must be a Python float: a tensor triggers a host sync.
+PER_TOKEN_ACTIVATION_GLOBAL_SCALE = 1.0 / (FLOAT8_E4M3_MAX * FLOAT4_E2M1_MAX)
+# GEMM K/N padding: the CuTe DSL grouped GEMMs need N % 128 and full 256-wide FP4 K tiles.
+_ALIGNMENT = 256
+# Gated FC1 rows are [up, gate] blocks of this many rows each, alternating.
+_GLU_INTERLEAVE_ROWS = 64
+
+_CUTE_DSL_WRAPPERS: dict = {}
+
+
+def require_flashinfer_routed_nvfp4() -> None:
+    """Raise an error when the per-token NVFP4 routed-MoE APIs are unavailable."""
+    if not HAVE_FLASHINFER_ROUTED_NVFP4:
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            "FlashInfer per-token NVFP4 MoE requires FlashInfer >= 0.7.0 with "
+            "nvidia-cutlass-dsl. Upgrade flashinfer-python or disable "
+            "inference_moe_nvfp4_recipe."
+        ) from _FLASHINFER_NVFP4_IMPORT_ERROR
+
+
+def _round_up(value: int, alignment: int) -> int:
+    return (value + alignment - 1) // alignment * alignment
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class FlashInferRoutedNVFP4Weights:
+    """FC1/FC2 expert stacks in the CuTe DSL block-scaled grouped-GEMM layout.
+
+    Data is packed E2M1 ``[experts, N, K // 2]``. ``*_scale`` is the 6D MMA view
+    of the 128x4-swizzled E4M3 block scales held in ``*_scale_swizzled``.
+    ``*_alpha`` are the per-expert FP32 dequantization scales and
+    ``fc2_input_scale`` is the per-token recipe constant for the FC2 input.
+    Gated (SwiGLU) FC1 has ``2 * padded_intermediate_size`` rows in FlashInfer's
+    interleaved up/gate order.
+    """
+
+    hidden_size: int
+    intermediate_size: int
+    padded_hidden_size: int
+    padded_intermediate_size: int
+    gated: bool
+    fc1_data: torch.Tensor
+    fc1_scale_swizzled: torch.Tensor
+    fc1_scale: torch.Tensor
+    fc1_alpha: torch.Tensor
+    fc2_data: torch.Tensor
+    fc2_scale_swizzled: torch.Tensor
+    fc2_scale: torch.Tensor
+    fc2_alpha: torch.Tensor
+    fc2_input_scale: torch.Tensor
+
+    @property
+    def num_local_experts(self) -> int:
+        """Number of experts in each stack."""
+        return self.fc1_data.shape[0]
+
+
+def _global_encode_scale(weight: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Return the one-element NVFP4 global encode scale for a weight matrix."""
+    amax = weight.abs().amax().float().reshape(1)
+    encode = (FLOAT8_E4M3_MAX * FLOAT4_E2M1_MAX) / amax
+    return torch.where(amax > 0, encode, torch.ones_like(encode))
+
+
+def _zero_pad(weight: torch.Tensor, padded_rows: int, padded_cols: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+    rows, cols = weight.shape
+    padded = weight.new_zeros(padded_rows, padded_cols, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    padded[:rows, :cols].copy_(weight)
+    return padded
+
+
+def _pad_fc1(weight: torch.Tensor, gated: bool, padded_i: int, padded_h: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Zero-pad one FC1 expert weight into the CuTe DSL row order.
+
+    MCore stores gated FC1 as ``[gate; up]``. FlashInfer expects ``[up; gate]`` with each half
+    padded separately and the halves interleaved in ``_GLU_INTERLEAVE_ROWS``-row blocks.
+    """
+    if not gated:
+        return _zero_pad(weight, padded_i, padded_h)
+    gate, up = weight.chunk(2, dim=0)
+    halves = torch.stack((_zero_pad(up, padded_i, padded_h), _zero_pad(gate, padded_i, padded_h)))
+    blocks = halves.view(2, padded_i // _GLU_INTERLEAVE_ROWS, _GLU_INTERLEAVE_ROWS, padded_h)
+    return blocks.transpose(0, 1).reshape(2 * padded_i, padded_h)
+
+
+def _quantize_expert(
+    padded: torch.Tensor,
+    data_out: torch.Tensor,
+    swizzled_scale_out: torch.Tensor,
+    alpha_out: torch.Tensor,
+) -> None:
+    """Quantize one zero-padded ``[rows, cols]`` expert weight into CuTe DSL NVFP4 storage."""
+    padded_rows, padded_cols = padded.shape
+    encode = _global_encode_scale(padded)
+    data, scale = nvfp4_quantize(padded, encode, sfLayout=SfLayout.layout_128x4)
+    data_out.copy_(data.view(torch.uint8).reshape(padded_rows, padded_cols // 2))
+    swizzled_scale_out.copy_(
+        scale.view(torch.uint8).reshape(padded_rows, padded_cols // NVFP4_BLOCK_SIZE)
+    )
+    alpha_out.copy_(encode.reciprocal())
+
+
+def _validate_stacks(
+    fc1_weight: torch.Tensor, fc2_weight: torch.Tensor
+) -> tuple[int, int, int, bool]:
+    """Return (experts, intermediate, hidden, gated); gated FC1 has twice FC2's input width."""
+    if fc1_weight.ndim != 3 or fc2_weight.ndim != 3:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "expected [experts, M, K] expert stacks, got "
+            f"fc1={tuple(fc1_weight.shape)}, fc2={tuple(fc2_weight.shape)}"
+        )
+    experts, hidden_size, intermediate_size = fc2_weight.shape
+    fc1_rows = fc1_weight.shape[1]
+    gated = fc1_rows == 2 * intermediate_size
+    if tuple(fc1_weight.shape) != (experts, fc1_rows, hidden_size) or fc1_rows not in (
+        intermediate_size,
+        2 * intermediate_size,
+    ):
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"FC1 shape {tuple(fc1_weight.shape)} does not match FC2 shape "
+            f"{tuple(fc2_weight.shape)}: expected [experts, intermediate or 2 * intermediate, "
+            "hidden]"
+        )
+    return experts, intermediate_size, hidden_size, gated
+
+
+def _check_refresh_metadata(
+    out, experts, hidden_size, intermediate_size, padded_h, padded_i, gated
+):
+    expected = (experts, hidden_size, intermediate_size, padded_h, padded_i, gated)
+    actual = (
+        out.num_local_experts,
+        out.hidden_size,
+        out.intermediate_size,
+        out.padded_hidden_size,
+        out.padded_intermediate_size,
+        out.gated,
+    )
+    if actual != expected:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "existing FlashInfer routed NVFP4 weight metadata changed across refit: "
+            f"got {actual}, expected {expected}"
+        )
+
+
+@torch.no_grad()
+def prepare_routed_nvfp4_weights(
+    fc1_weight: torch.Tensor,
+    fc2_weight: torch.Tensor,
+    out: FlashInferRoutedNVFP4Weights | None = None,
+) -> FlashInferRoutedNVFP4Weights:
+    """Quantize BF16 squared-ReLU or SwiGLU expert stacks into the per-token NVFP4 kernel layout.
+
+    Args:
+        fc1_weight: ``[experts, intermediate, hidden]`` BF16 FC1 weights, or
+            ``[experts, 2 * intermediate, hidden]`` as MCore's ``[gate; up]`` for SwiGLU.
+        fc2_weight: ``[experts, hidden, intermediate]`` BF16 FC2 weights.
+        out: When provided, its tensors are refreshed in place. This preserves
+            addresses captured by CUDA graphs across model refits.
+    """
+    require_flashinfer_routed_nvfp4()
+    experts, intermediate_size, hidden_size, gated = _validate_stacks(fc1_weight, fc2_weight)
+    padded_h = _round_up(hidden_size, _ALIGNMENT)
+    padded_i = _round_up(intermediate_size, _ALIGNMENT)
+    fc1_rows = 2 * padded_i if gated else padded_i
+    device = fc1_weight.device
+
+    if out is None:
+
+        def _empty(*shape, dtype):
+            return torch.empty(*shape, dtype=dtype, device=device)
+
+        # Each expert's row count is a multiple of 128, so per-expert 128x4-swizzled
+        # scale blocks concatenate into the swizzled layout of the stacked matrix.
+        fc1_scale_swizzled = _empty(
+            experts * fc1_rows, padded_h // NVFP4_BLOCK_SIZE, dtype=torch.uint8
+        )
+        fc2_scale_swizzled = _empty(
+            experts * padded_h, padded_i // NVFP4_BLOCK_SIZE, dtype=torch.uint8
+        )
+        out = FlashInferRoutedNVFP4Weights(
+            hidden_size=hidden_size,
+            intermediate_size=intermediate_size,
+            padded_hidden_size=padded_h,
+            padded_intermediate_size=padded_i,
+            gated=gated,
+            fc1_data=_empty(experts, fc1_rows, padded_h // 2, dtype=torch.uint8),
+            fc1_scale_swizzled=fc1_scale_swizzled,
+            fc1_scale=convert_sf_to_mma_layout(
+                fc1_scale_swizzled, m=fc1_rows, k=padded_h, num_groups=experts
+            ),
+            fc1_alpha=_empty(experts, dtype=torch.float32),
+            fc2_data=_empty(experts, padded_h, padded_i // 2, dtype=torch.uint8),
+            fc2_scale_swizzled=fc2_scale_swizzled,
+            fc2_scale=convert_sf_to_mma_layout(
+                fc2_scale_swizzled, m=padded_h, k=padded_i, num_groups=experts
+            ),
+            fc2_alpha=_empty(experts, dtype=torch.float32),
+            fc2_input_scale=torch.full(
+                (1,), PER_TOKEN_ACTIVATION_GLOBAL_SCALE, dtype=torch.float32, device=device
+            ),
+        )
+    else:
+        _check_refresh_metadata(
+            out, experts, hidden_size, intermediate_size, padded_h, padded_i, gated
+        )
+
+    for expert in range(experts):
+        _quantize_expert(
+            _pad_fc1(fc1_weight[expert], gated, padded_i, padded_h),
+            out.fc1_data[expert],
+            out.fc1_scale_swizzled[expert * fc1_rows : (expert + 1) * fc1_rows],
+            out.fc1_alpha[expert : expert + 1],
+        )
+        _quantize_expert(
+            _zero_pad(fc2_weight[expert], padded_h, padded_i),
+            out.fc2_data[expert],
+            out.fc2_scale_swizzled[expert * padded_h : (expert + 1) * padded_h],
+            out.fc2_alpha[expert : expert + 1],
+        )
+    for swizzled, mma, m, k in (
+        (out.fc1_scale_swizzled, out.fc1_scale, fc1_rows, padded_h),
+        (out.fc2_scale_swizzled, out.fc2_scale, padded_h, padded_i),
+    ):
+        converted = convert_sf_to_mma_layout(swizzled, m=m, k=k, num_groups=experts)
+        if converted.data_ptr() != mma.data_ptr():
+            mma.copy_(converted)
+    return out
+
+
+def quantize_routed_nvfp4_input(
+    hidden_states: torch.Tensor, padded_hidden_size: int
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    """Pad and quantize routed-MoE input with one FP32 scale per token.
+
+    Returns packed E2M1 data ``[tokens, padded_hidden // 2]``, linear block scales
+    ``[tokens, padded_hidden // 16]`` (as returned by FlashInfer), and FP32
+    per-token scales ``[tokens]``.
+    """
+    hidden_padding = padded_hidden_size - hidden_states.shape[-1]
+    if hidden_padding < 0:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"padded hidden size {padded_hidden_size} is smaller than input hidden size "
+            f"{hidden_states.shape[-1]}"
+        )
+    padded_hidden = F.pad(hidden_states, (0, hidden_padding)) if hidden_padding else hidden_states
+    quantized_hidden, hidden_scale, per_token_scale = nvfp4_quantize(
+        padded_hidden.contiguous(),
+        PER_TOKEN_ACTIVATION_GLOBAL_SCALE,
+        sfLayout=SfLayout.layout_linear,
+        per_token_activation=True,
+    )
+    hidden_scale = hidden_scale.reshape(
+        hidden_states.shape[0], padded_hidden_size // NVFP4_BLOCK_SIZE
+    )
+    return quantized_hidden, hidden_scale, per_token_scale
+
+
+def _get_cute_dsl_wrapper(
+    weights: FlashInferRoutedNVFP4Weights,
+    num_experts: int,
+    top_k: int,
+    local_expert_offset: int,
+    activation_type: int,
+    device: torch.device,
+):
+    # The fused finalize accumulates top-k routes with output-dtype atomics, whose
+    # order is not fixed; the two-stage finalize reduces each token's routes in order.
+    use_fused_finalize = not (
+        torch.are_deterministic_algorithms_enabled() or is_batch_invariant_mode_enabled()
+    )
+    key = (
+        use_fused_finalize,
+        num_experts,
+        top_k,
+        weights.padded_hidden_size,

+"""DSA attention and lightning-indexer FLOPs accounting."""
+
+import math
+
+from megatron.core.models.hybrid.hybrid_layer_allocation import Symbols, parse_hybrid_pattern
+from megatron.core.transformer.experimental_attention_variant.dsa import is_dsa_skip_topk_layer
+
+
+def _dsa_sparse_core_scale(total_real_tokens, seqlen_squared_sum, dsa_indexer_topk):
+    """Fraction of dense causal (query, key) pairs that DSA actually attends to.
+
+    A DSA layer scores every past position with the indexer but runs attention
+    only over the ``dsa_indexer_topk`` highest-scoring keys, so its core
+    attention cost is ``sum_i(min(i, topk))`` pairs per sequence instead of the
+    dense causal ``L^2 / 2``. Returns the ratio between the two, i.e. the
+    factor the dense core-attention coefficient must be scaled by.
+
+    The caller only has the batch aggregates ``sum_i(L_i)`` and
+    ``sum_i(L_i ** 2)``, not the individual sequence lengths, so the ratio is
+    evaluated at the length-weighted mean ``sum(L^2) / sum(L)``. For equal-length
+    sequences, this aggregation introduces no additional approximation, but
+    the pair counts still use the continuous approximation described below.
+    For ragged batches, it weights toward the long sequences that dominate
+    attention cost. Collapses to ``1.0`` when the sequences are
+    no longer than ``topk``, where top-k selects everything and attention is
+    dense.
+    """
+    if not dsa_indexer_topk or total_real_tokens <= 0 or seqlen_squared_sum <= 0:
+        return 1.0
+    mean_seqlen = seqlen_squared_sum / total_real_tokens
+    # Average attended KV entries per query: ``min(i, topk)`` averaged over the
+    # sequence, approximated as ``eff * (1 - eff / (2 * L))`` with
+    # ``eff = min(topk, floor(L))``. The exact discrete average has ``eff - 1``
+    # in the correction term; the O(1/L) difference is below the precision of
+    # this estimate.
+    eff = min(dsa_indexer_topk, math.floor(mean_seqlen))
+    attended = eff * (1 - eff / (2 * mean_seqlen))
+    # Dense causal attention averages ~``mean_seqlen / 2`` keys per query.
+    return attended / (mean_seqlen / 2)
+
+
+def _dsa_kpool_pairs(mean_seqlen, pool_size, max_pools=None):
+    """Sum complete causal pools per query, optionally capped by selection.
+
+    Interpolate adjacent integer lengths for a fractional length-weighted mean;
+    individual document boundaries cannot be recovered from batch aggregates.
+    """
+    length = math.floor(mean_seqlen)
+    pools, next_pools = length // pool_size, (length + 1) // pool_size
+    if max_pools is not None:
+        pools, next_pools = min(pools, max_pools), min(next_pools, max_pools)
+    return (
+        pool_size * pools * (pools - 1) / 2
+        + pools * (length - pool_size * pools + 1)
+        + (mean_seqlen - length) * next_pools
+    )
+
+
+def _dsa_kpool_attention_scale(
+    total_tokens: float,
+    seqlen_squared_sum: float,
+    topk: int | None,
+    pool_size: int,
+    always_select_tail: bool,
+) -> float:
+    """Return the selected attention-pair fraction for pooled keys.
+
+    Expand at most topk / pool_size complete pools to tokens and optionally
+    append the incomplete tail. Normalize by discrete dense pairs so a dense
+    selection retains the caller's existing L^2 / 2 FLOPs convention.
+    """
+    if topk is None or topk <= 0 or topk % pool_size:
+        raise ValueError("KPool FLOPs require a positive top-k divisible by the pool size.")
+    if total_tokens <= 0 or seqlen_squared_sum <= 0:
+        return 0.0
+    mean_seqlen = seqlen_squared_sum / total_tokens
+    length = math.floor(mean_seqlen)
+    fraction = mean_seqlen - length
+    pools, tail = divmod(length, pool_size)
+    attention_pairs = pool_size * _dsa_kpool_pairs(mean_seqlen, pool_size, topk // pool_size)
+    if always_select_tail:
+        attention_pairs += (
+            pools * pool_size * (pool_size - 1) / 2
+            + tail * (tail + 1) / 2
+            + fraction * ((length + 1) % pool_size)
+        )
+    dense_pairs = length * (length + 1) / 2 + fraction * (length + 1)
+    return attention_pairs / dense_pairs
+
+
+def _dsa_indexer_flops(
+    *,
+    total_tokens,
+    seqlen_squared_sum,
+    hidden_size,
+    q_lora_rank,
+    n_heads,
+    head_dim,
+    num_indexer_layers,
+    dsa_indexer_loss_enabled: bool,
+    dsa_indexer_use_sparse_loss=False,
+    dsa_indexer_topk=None,

+):
+    """DSA lightning-indexer FLOPs coefficients, fwd/bwd expansion included.
+
+    Only actual indexer executions pay. Without KL loss, all work is forward
+    only. With loss, detached projection inputs require fwd + wgrad (x2),
+    while scoring requires dense fwd + dq + dk: x3 for dense KL, or
+    ``1 + 2 * sparse_scale`` for sparse KL. This counts model FLOPs, excluding
+    zero-padded work in the dense reference implementation of sparse backward.
+
+    KPool is forward only: add its gate and complete-pool key reduction, and
+    score complete pools instead of individual keys. Pool softmax, positional
+    bias, top-k selection, teacher recomputation and KL operations are excluded.
+
+    Returns ``(token_linear, core)`` including FMA x2 and backward factors;
+    the caller multiplies by total tokens and sum(L^2), respectively.
+    """
+    if dsa_indexer_kpool > 1:
+        if dsa_indexer_loss_enabled:
+            raise ValueError("KPool FLOPs require indexer loss to be disabled, as in DSAttention.")
+        if (
+            dsa_indexer_topk is None
+            or dsa_indexer_topk <= 0
+            or dsa_indexer_topk % dsa_indexer_kpool
+        ):
+            raise ValueError("KPool FLOPs require a positive top-k divisible by the pool size.")
+    if num_indexer_layers <= 0:
+        return 0, 0
+    if q_lora_rank is None:
+        # Mirrors DSAIndexer's own fallback when the model has no q lora rank.
+        q_lora_rank = hidden_size
+    index_dim = n_heads * head_dim
+    token_linear = num_indexer_layers * (
+        q_lora_rank * index_dim  # wq_b
+        + hidden_size * head_dim  # wk
+        + hidden_size * n_heads  # weights_proj
+    )
+    # Scoring each query against every past token under a causal mask (/2).
+    core = num_indexer_layers * index_dim / 2
+    fma_expansion_factor = 2
+    core_expansion: float
+    if not dsa_indexer_loss_enabled:
+        token_expansion, core_expansion = 1, 1
+    else:
+        # Projections: fwd + wgrad (input is detached, no dgrad).
+        token_expansion = 2
+        # Scoring: dense fwd + dq + dk, where dq/dk cover only the top-k pairs
+        # under the sparse KL loss (see docstring).
+        sparse_core_scale = (
+            _dsa_sparse_core_scale(total_tokens, seqlen_squared_sum, dsa_indexer_topk)
+            if dsa_indexer_use_sparse_loss
+            else 1.0
+        )
+        core_expansion = 1 + 2 * sparse_core_scale
+    token_linear = token_expansion * fma_expansion_factor * token_linear
+    core = core_expansion * fma_expansion_factor * core
+    if dsa_indexer_kpool > 1:
+        indexer_scale = compression_scale = 0.0
+        if total_tokens > 0 and seqlen_squared_sum > 0:
+            mean_seqlen = seqlen_squared_sum / total_tokens
+            length = math.floor(mean_seqlen)
+            fraction = mean_seqlen - length
+            pool_size = dsa_indexer_kpool
+            pools, next_pools = length // pool_size, (length + 1) // pool_size
+            dense_pairs = length * (length + 1) / 2 + fraction * (length + 1)
+            indexer_scale = _dsa_kpool_pairs(mean_seqlen, pool_size) / dense_pairs
+            compression_scale = pool_size * (pools + fraction * (next_pools - pools)) / mean_seqlen
+        # Gate on every token; one FMA per key component in complete pools.
+        token_linear += 2 * num_indexer_layers * head_dim * (hidden_size + compression_scale)
+        core *= indexer_scale
+    return token_linear, core
+
+
+def _num_dsa_indexer_layers(num_layers, skip_topk_offset, topk_freq):
+    """Count indexer executions in a block numbered from 1 to ``num_layers``."""
+    return sum(
+        1
+        for layer_number in range(1, num_layers + 1)
+        if not is_dsa_skip_topk_layer(layer_number, skip_topk_offset or 0, topk_freq or 1)
+    )
+
+
+def _num_dsa_indexer_layers_in_pattern(layer_types, dsa_symbol, skip_topk_offset, topk_freq):
+    """Count hybrid DSA positions that compute their own index.
+
+    The caller supplies one block with pipes stripped. Non-DSA positions
+    advance the 1-based layer numbering used by DSAttention's skip predicate.
+    """
+    return sum(
+        1
+        for layer_number, symbol in enumerate(layer_types, start=1)
+        if symbol == dsa_symbol
+        and not is_dsa_skip_topk_layer(layer_number, skip_topk_offset or 0, topk_freq or 1)
+    )
+
+
+def dsa_layer_flops(
+    total_tokens: float,
+    seqlen_squared_sum: float,
+    hidden_size: int,
+    num_attention_heads: int,
+    q_lora_rank: int | None,
+    kv_lora_rank: int,
+    qk_head_dim: int,
+    qk_pos_emb_head_dim: int,
+    v_head_dim: int,
+    dsa_indexer_topk: int | None,
+    dsa_indexer_kpool: int = 1,
+    dsa_indexer_kpool_always_select_tail: bool = True,
+) -> float:
+    """Calculate forward FLOPs for one DSA attention layer, excluding its indexer.
+
+    Like the other layer counters, the result includes the FMA factor of two
+    and the batch token statistics, but no backward expansion or layer count.
+    Callers multiply by the number of DSA layers and apply their common x3
+    forward/backward expansion.
+
+    Token-linear work includes the MLA projections and their norm estimates.
+    Core attention uses the absorbed KV dimensions and top-k sparse pair scale.
+    The indexer is accounted for separately by ``dsa_indexer_flops`` because
+    its executed layer count and backward cost can differ from attention.
+    With KPool, only complete pools are selected and expanded to original
+    tokens; the tail flag controls additional incomplete-pool tokens.
+    """
+    if q_lora_rank is None:
+        q_term = hidden_size * num_attention_heads * (qk_head_dim + qk_pos_emb_head_dim)
+    else:
+        q_term = q_lora_rank * (
+            hidden_size + num_attention_heads * (qk_head_dim + qk_pos_emb_head_dim) + 1
+        )
+    fma_expansion_factor = 2
+    token_linear = fma_expansion_factor * (
+        ## q lora + rope + q norm
+        q_term
+        ## kv lora + rope + kv norm
+        + kv_lora_rank * (hidden_size + num_attention_heads * (qk_head_dim + v_head_dim) + 1)
+        + hidden_size * qk_pos_emb_head_dim
+        ## o proj
+        + (num_attention_heads * v_head_dim) * hidden_size
+    )
+    if dsa_indexer_kpool > 1:
+        sparse_core_scale = _dsa_kpool_attention_scale(
+            total_tokens,
+            seqlen_squared_sum,
+            dsa_indexer_topk,
+            dsa_indexer_kpool,
+            dsa_indexer_kpool_always_select_tail,
+        )
+    else:
+        sparse_core_scale = _dsa_sparse_core_scale(
+            total_tokens, seqlen_squared_sum, dsa_indexer_topk
+        )
+    core = (
+        fma_expansion_factor
+        * (
+            num_attention_heads * (kv_lora_rank + qk_pos_emb_head_dim) / 2
+            + num_attention_heads * kv_lora_rank / 2
+        )
+        * sparse_core_scale
+    )
+    return total_tokens * token_linear + seqlen_squared_sum * core
+
+
+def dsa_indexer_flops(

+    seqlen_squared_sum: float,

+    dsa_indexer_head_dim: int,

+def parse_tensor_metric_specs(specifications: Sequence[str]) -> tuple[ScheduledMetric, ...]:
+    """Parse configured tensor metrics in `NAME:INTERVAL` form.
+
+    Args:
+        specifications: Metric names paired with positive iteration intervals.
+
+    Returns:
+        Scheduled metric instances in configuration order.
+
+    Raises:
+        ValueError: If a specification is malformed, duplicated, unknown, or has an invalid
+            interval.
+    """
+    scheduled_metrics = []
+    configured_names = set()
+    available_names = ", ".join(sorted(_TENSOR_METRIC_FACTORIES))
+    for specification in specifications:
+        name, separator, interval_text = specification.strip().rpartition(":")
+        if not separator or not name or not interval_text:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"Invalid tensor metric specification {specification!r}; expected NAME:INTERVAL."
+            )
+        if name not in _TENSOR_METRIC_FACTORIES:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"Unknown tensor metric {name!r}; available tensor metrics: {available_names}."
+            )
+        if name in configured_names:
+            raise ValueError(f"Tensor metric {name!r} was configured more than once.")
+        try:
+            interval = int(interval_text)
+        except ValueError as error:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"Tensor metric {name!r} requires an integer interval, got {interval_text!r}."
+            ) from error
+        if interval <= 0:
+            raise ValueError(f"Tensor metric {name!r} requires a positive interval.")
+        configured_names.add(name)
+        scheduled_metrics.append(ScheduledMetric(_TENSOR_METRIC_FACTORIES[name](), interval))
+    return tuple(scheduled_metrics)

+class TrainingTensorMetricObserver:

+

+    independent of the observed tensor; partial CUDA graphs may reuse an output buffer after the
+    callback returns. Parameter metrics observe optimizer/master values when locally available,
+    and wgrad metrics observe finalized `main_grad` or `grad` values at that commit point.
+    Ordinary, Distributed, LayerWise, and Chained optimizer storage is represented explicitly
+    across tensor, expert, data, and expert-data parallel axes. GTP-rematerialized parameter and
+    wgrad shards have physical padding removed by the optimizer source. Pipeline parallelism,

+    def _due_metrics(self, iteration: int) -> tuple[ScheduledMetric, ...]:

+    def _validate_metric_sources(scheduled_metrics: Sequence[ScheduledMetric]) -> None:

+            for scheduled in scheduled_metrics

+                f"declare source_kinds; missing declarations: {sorted(undeclared_sources)}."

+def _forward_rank_relations(
+    tp_shard_dim: int | None,
+    sequence_dim: int | None,
+    batch_dim: int | None,
+    pg_collection: ProcessGroupCollection,
+) -> tuple[RankRelation, ...]:
+    """Describe a forward tensor over tensor, context, GTP, and data parallel ranks."""
+    tp_group = getattr(pg_collection, "tp", None)
+    cp_group = getattr(pg_collection, "cp", None)
+    gtp_group = getattr(pg_collection, "gtp_remat", None)
+    dp_group = getattr(pg_collection, "dp", None)
+    if tp_group is None or cp_group is None or gtp_group is None or dp_group is None:
+        raise ValueError("Forward tensor metrics require tp, cp, gtp_remat, and dp process groups.")
+    tp_placement = (
+        Shard(tp_shard_dim) if tp_shard_dim is not None and tp_group.size() > 1 else Replica()
+    )
+    # CP, GTP, and DP ranks always carry distinct activation populations. If a source cannot name
+    # their tensor dimension, preserve that fact as Shard(None) rather than calling it a replica.
+    cp_placement = Shard(sequence_dim) if cp_group.size() > 1 else Replica()
+    gtp_placement = Shard(batch_dim) if gtp_group.size() > 1 else Replica()
+    dp_placement = Shard(batch_dim) if dp_group.size() > 1 else Replica()
+    return (
+        RankRelation("tp", tp_placement),
+        RankRelation("cp", cp_placement),
+        RankRelation("gtp", gtp_placement),
+        RankRelation("dp", dp_placement),
+    )

+    for model_chunk in model:
+        config = getattr(unwrap_model(model_chunk), "config", None)
+        cuda_graph_impl = getattr(config, "cuda_graph_impl", "none")
+        if cuda_graph_impl == "full_iteration":
+            raise NotImplementedError(
+                "Forward tensor metrics do not yet support full-iteration CUDA graphs."
+            )
+        if source_kinds.isdisjoint(
+            {"router_logits", "router_scores", "router_diagnostics"}
+        ) or cuda_graph_impl not in {"local", "transformer_engine"}:
+            continue
+        graph_modules = tuple(getattr(config, "cuda_graph_modules", ()))
+        if not graph_modules or any(
+            graph_module
+            in {CudaGraphModule.moe, CudaGraphModule.moe_router, CudaGraphModule.moe_preprocess}
+            for graph_module in graph_modules
+        ):

+                "Router tensor metrics require an eager MoE router; disable moe, "

+    """Bind abstract metric axes to caller-supplied process groups."""
+    groups = {}
+    for axis, attribute in (
+        ("tp", "tp"),
+        ("expert_tp", "expt_tp"),
+        ("ep", "ep"),
+        ("cp", "cp"),
+        ("gtp", "gtp_remat"),
+        ("expert_gtp", "expt_gtp_remat"),

+# Copyright (c) 2026 NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved.
+
+"""Exercise the real GPT train/evaluate loop with static or runtime-CP packed data.
+
+This is a smoke/coverage test, not a deterministic or golden-loss equivalence test.
+The worker observes batch metadata without replacing training or collectives.
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import json
+import math
+import os
+import re
+import runpy
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import tempfile
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import yaml
+
+CASE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+REPO_ROOT = CASE_DIR.parents[4]
+
+
+def run_worker() -> None:
+    """Run the unmodified GPT entrypoint and record which CP sizes it consumes."""
+    import torch
+
+    from megatron.core.datasets import data_schedule
+
+    original_get_batch = data_schedule.get_batch_on_this_rank_for_sequence_packing
+    observed = {"train": set(), "eval": set()}
+
+    def observe_batch(*args, **kwargs):
+        result = original_get_batch(*args, **kwargs)
+        packed = result[5]
+        group = packed.cp_group
+        cp_size = 1 if group is None else group.size()
+        if kwargs.get("dynamic_cp", False):
+            assert group is not None, "Runtime CP1 must retain its singleton process group"
+            assert packed.local_cp_size == cp_size
+        phase = "train" if torch.is_grad_enabled() else "eval"
+        observed[phase].add(cp_size)
+        return result
+
+    data_schedule.get_batch_on_this_rank_for_sequence_packing = observe_batch
+    sys.argv = [str(REPO_ROOT / "pretrain_gpt.py"), *sys.argv[2:]]
+    runpy.run_path(sys.argv[0], run_name="__main__")
+    output = Path(os.environ["DCP_TEST_OBSERVATIONS"])
+    output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    (output / f"rank-{os.environ['RANK']}.json").write_text(
+        json.dumps({phase: sorted(sizes) for phase, sizes in observed.items()}), encoding="utf-8"
+    )
+
+
+def run_test() -> None:
+    """Launch eight ranks, then check real losses, checkpoints, and runtime groups."""
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--packing-mode", choices=("static", "dynamic"), required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--output-path", type=Path, required=True)
+    options = parser.parse_args()
+    output_root = options.output_path.resolve()
+    output_root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    # Preserve failed artifacts while permitting the CI runner to retry a workload.
+    output = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="attempt-", dir=output_root))
+    config = yaml.safe_load((CASE_DIR / "model_config.yaml").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+    model_args = config["MODEL_ARGS"]
+    model_args.update(
+        {
+            "--sequence-packing-scheduler": (
+                "default_dynamic_cp" if options.packing_mode == "dynamic" else "dp_balanced"
+            ),
+            "--max-seqlen-per-dp-cp-rank": 1024 if options.packing_mode == "dynamic" else 2048,
+            "--varlen-mock-dataset-config-json": json.dumps(
+                {"mode": "file", "path": str(CASE_DIR / "lengths.csv")}
+            ),
+            "--save": str(output / "checkpoints"),
+        }
+    )
+    if options.packing_mode == "dynamic":
+        model_args["--dynamic-context-parallel"] = True
+    arguments = []
+    for name, value in model_args.items():
+        if value is not False and value is not None:
+            arguments.append(name)
+            if value is not True:
+                arguments.append(str(value))
+    environment = dict(os.environ)
+    environment.update({name: str(value) for name, value in config["ENV_VARS"].items()})
+    environment["DCP_TEST_OBSERVATIONS"] = str(output / "observations")
+    environment["PYTHONPATH"] = str(REPO_ROOT) + os.pathsep + environment.get("PYTHONPATH", "")
+    environment["OMP_NUM_THREADS"] = "1"
+    command = [
+        sys.executable,
+        "-m",
+        "torch.distributed.run",
+        "--standalone",
+        "--nproc-per-node=8",
+        str(Path(__file__).resolve()),
+        "--worker",
+        *arguments,
+    ]
+    log_path = output / "training.log"
+    try:
+        with log_path.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as log:
+            subprocess.run(
+                command,
+                cwd=REPO_ROOT,
+                env=environment,
+                stdout=log,
+                stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
+                check=True,
+                timeout=900,
+            )
+    except (subprocess.CalledProcessError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
+        print(f"Training failed; full per-rank output: {log_path}", file=sys.stderr)
+        print("\n".join(log_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()[-80:]), file=sys.stderr)
+        raise
+    log_text = log_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
+    for pattern, minimum in (
+        (r"\blm loss:\s*([^\s|]+)", model_args["--train-iters"]),
+        (r"\blm loss value:\s*([^\s|]+)", 2),
+        (r"\bgrad norm:\s*([^\s|]+)", model_args["--train-iters"]),
+    ):
+        values = [float(value) for value in re.findall(pattern, log_text)]
+        assert len(values) >= minimum, f"Missing train/eval metrics in {log_path}: {pattern}"
+        assert all(math.isfinite(value) for value in values), f"Non-finite metrics in {log_path}"
+    tracker = output / "checkpoints" / "latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt"
+    assert int(tracker.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) == model_args["--train-iters"]
+    expected_sizes = {1, 2} if options.packing_mode == "dynamic" else {1}
+    for phase in ("train", "eval"):
+        sizes = set()
+        for rank in range(8):
+            observation = json.loads(
+                (output / "observations" / f"rank-{rank}.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
+            )
+            assert observation[phase], f"Rank {rank} did not consume {phase} packed data"
+            sizes.update(observation[phase])
+        assert sizes == expected_sizes, f"{phase}: expected CP {expected_sizes}, saw {sizes}"
+    print(f"Packed {options.packing_mode} GPT train/eval passed; artifacts: {output}")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    if len(sys.argv) > 1 and sys.argv[1] == "--worker":
+        run_worker()
+    else:
+        run_test()

+def _scheduler_return(module):
+    """Build a metadata-free scheduler result for the entrypoint under test.
+
+    NOTE(nightly-sync 26_10_2026): get_batch now calls prepare_packed_seq_params on the
+    scheduler's result (dev-only frontend hook, restored on main's structure), so an opaque
+    object() sentinel no longer survives the handoff -- gpt reads index 5 and hybrid calls
+    get_packed_seq_params(). The metadata is None on purpose: with real PackedSeqParams,
+    finalize_packed_seq_params would read parallel_state.get_context_parallel_group and trip
+    this module's own "must not read parallel_state" guard. Each test still asserts that
+    get_batch returns this exact object.
+    """
+    if module is pretrain_hybrid:

+    return (None,) * 7

+class _Wrapper:

+class _RouterDecoder:
+    """Exercise HybridModel's layout masks with real GPU/SP groups and MoE routing."""

+    def __init__(self, cp_batch, pg_collection, config):
+        self.cp_batch = cp_batch
+        self.pg_collection = pg_collection
+        self.router = TopKRouter(config=config, pg_collection=pg_collection).cuda()
+        self.router.set_layer_number(1)

+    def __call__(self, hidden_states, padding_mask_by_layout, **kwargs):
+        for layout, batch in self.cp_batch.batches_by_layout.items():
+            cp_mask = batch['padding_mask']
+            expected = cp_mask.chunk(self.pg_collection.tp.size(), dim=1)[
+                self.pg_collection.tp.rank()
+            ]
+            mask = padding_mask_by_layout[layout]
+            torch.testing.assert_close(mask, expected)
+            # Derive the activation shape from the CP batch, not the mask under test.
+            tokens = batch['tokens'] if batch['tokens'] is not None else batch['labels']
+            local_tokens = tokens.shape[1] // self.pg_collection.tp.size()
+            activations = torch.randn(local_tokens, 1, 8, device='cuda', requires_grad=True)
+            probs, _ = self.router(
+                activations,
+                padding_mask=mask.transpose(0, 1).contiguous(),
+                packed_seq_params=self.cp_batch.get_packed_seq_params(layout),
+            )
+            probs.square().sum().backward()
+            assert torch.isfinite(activations.grad).all()
+            assert torch.isfinite(self.router.weight.grad).all()
+            self.router.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
+        return hidden_states if hidden_states is not None else self.input_tensor

+def _group(size, rank=0, stride=1):
+    return SimpleNamespace(
+        size=lambda: size, rank=lambda: rank, ranks=list(range(0, size * stride, stride))
+    )

+def _batch(lengths):
+    lengths = torch.tensor(lengths, dtype=torch.int32)
+    boundaries = torch.cat((lengths.new_zeros(1), lengths.cumsum(0, dtype=torch.int32)))
+    tokens = torch.arange(int(boundaries[-1]), dtype=torch.int64)
+    return {
+        "tokens": tokens.clone(),
+        "labels": tokens.clone() + 1,
+        "position_ids": tokens.clone(),
+        "loss_mask": torch.ones_like(tokens, dtype=torch.float32),
+        "cu_seqlens": boundaries.clone(),
+        "cu_seqlens_padded": boundaries.clone(),
+        "max_seqlen": lengths.max(),
+    }

+def test_capture_does_not_borrow_eager_wgrad_storage(monkeypatch):
+    """A graph must not keep a scratch address that eager work can later overwrite."""
+    Utils.initialize_distributed()
+    monkeypatch.setattr(gtp, "_wgrad_buf_pool", {})
+    eager = gtp._wgrad_pool_get((1024,), torch.float32, "cuda")
+    assert eager._from_gtp_wgrad_pool
+    gtp._wgrad_pool_put(eager)
+    result = torch.empty_like(eager)
+    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+        scratch = gtp._wgrad_pool_get(eager.shape, eager.dtype, eager.device)
+        scratch.fill_(3)
+        result.copy_(scratch)
+        # Graph-owned scratch is never cached for eager reuse, whatever release path sees it.

+        gtp._wgrad_pool_put(scratch)
+    assert scratch.data_ptr() != eager.data_ptr()
+    assert gtp._wgrad_pool_get(eager.shape, eager.dtype, eager.device) is eager
+    assert not gtp._wgrad_buf_pool.get((eager.shape, eager.dtype))
+    for _ in range(3):
+        eager.fill_(9)
+        graph.replay()
+        torch.testing.assert_close(result, torch.full_like(result, 3))

+"""Grouped reduce-scatter must release eager inputs before graph-only replay."""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from megatron.core.tensor_parallel import generalized_tensor_parallelism as gtp
+from tests.unit_tests.generalized_tensor_parallel.gtp_test_utils import (
+    _torchrun_dist_init,
+    reset_gtp_globals,
+)
+

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("async_op", [False, True])
+def test_grouped_rs_releases_inputs_after_wait(monkeypatch, async_op):
+    """Check input lifetime without issuing another collective to flush NCCL's shelf."""
+    group = torch.distributed.group.WORLD
+    if group.size() < 2:
+        pytest.skip("requires at least two GPUs")
+    monkeypatch.setattr(gtp.GTP_CONFIG, "reduce_scatter_with_fp32_accumulation", False)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(gtp.GTP_CONFIG, "calculate_per_token_loss", False)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(gtp.GTP_CONFIG, "check_param_states", False)
+    module = torch.nn.Module()
+    shape = (64 * group.size(), 64)
+    for name in ("weight0", "weight1"):
+        module.register_parameter(
+            name, torch.nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(shape, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda"))
+        )
+    gtp.wrap_module_params_gtp(module, ["weight0", "weight1"], group, is_grouped=True)
+    weight = module.weight0
+
+    def reduce(packed):
+        outputs, handle, release_bufs = weight._reduce_scatter(
+            list(packed.unbind()), async_op=async_op
+        )
+        if handle is not None:
+            handle.wait()
+        # Match the caller dropping its input references once the RS has completed.
+        del release_bufs
+        return outputs
+
+    # Use views into one packed allocation, as TE's grouped wgrad GEMM does.
+    packed = torch.full((2, *shape), group.rank() + 1, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+    address = packed.data_ptr()
+    outputs = reduce(packed)
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    expected = (group.size() + 1) / 2
+    for output in outputs:
+        torch.testing.assert_close(output, torch.full_like(output, expected), atol=0, rtol=0)
+    del packed
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    # Inspect storage, not Python weakrefs: a Work can retain TensorImpls in C++.
+    # Do not enqueue more collectives here; that can release an orphan Work's shelf
+    # and mask the retention that persists when training switches to graph replay.
+    for segment in torch.cuda.memory_snapshot():
+        for block in segment["blocks"]:
+            if block["address"] == address:
+                assert block["state"] != "active_allocated", "wait retained grouped RS input"
+
+    # Captured inputs must remain valid across replay, despite releasing eager inputs.
+    offset = torch.zeros((), dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+        packed = torch.empty((2, *shape), dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+        packed.fill_(group.rank() + 1).add_(offset)
+        outputs = reduce(packed)
+        del packed
+    for value in (0, 4, 8):
+        offset.fill_(value)
+        graph.replay()
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        for output in outputs:
+            torch.testing.assert_close(
+                output, torch.full_like(output, expected + value), atol=0, rtol=0
+            )

+def build_flashinfer_jit_in_rank_order():
+    """Builds FlashInfer's JIT modules one rank at a time before any test runs.
+
+    A cold build takes minutes and FlashInfer serializes it across processes, so ranks that
+    build inside the tests reach the multi-rank setups minutes apart, while the test

+def _reference_moe(hidden, fc1, fc2, topk_ids, topk_weights):
+    """BF16 squared-ReLU MoE, or SwiGLU when FC1 holds MCore's [gate; up] halves."""
+    gated = fc1.shape[1] == 2 * fc2.shape[2]
+    output = torch.zeros_like(hidden, dtype=torch.float32)
+    for slot in range(topk_ids.shape[1]):
+        for expert in range(fc1.shape[0]):
+            rows = topk_ids[:, slot] == expert
+            if not rows.any():
+                continue
+            fc1_out = hidden[rows].float() @ fc1[expert].float().t()
+            if gated:
+                gate, up = fc1_out.chunk(2, dim=-1)
+                intermediate = F.silu(gate) * up
+            else:
+                intermediate = F.relu(fc1_out).square()
+            expert_out = intermediate @ fc2[expert].float().t()
+            output[rows] += topk_weights[rows, slot : slot + 1] * expert_out
+    return output
+
+
+def _activation_type(gated):
+    from flashinfer import ActivationType
+
+    return (ActivationType.Swiglu if gated else ActivationType.Relu2).value

+def _assert_close_to_reference(output, reference):
+    # Exact NVFP4 emulation of these shapes gives per-token cosine ~0.98 mean and ~0.965 at
+    # worst; layout or scale bugs collapse it far below these bounds.
+    cosine = F.cosine_similarity(output.float(), reference, dim=-1)
+    assert cosine.mean().item() > 0.97, cosine.mean().item()
+    assert cosine.min().item() > 0.95, cosine.min().item()
+
+
+# E2M1 code -> value; bit 3 is the sign.
+_E2M1_MAGNITUDES = (0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0, 6.0)
+_E2M1_VALUES = _E2M1_MAGNITUDES + tuple(-value for value in _E2M1_MAGNITUDES)
+# (upper bound, bound inclusive, value): round-half-to-even onto the E2M1 grid.
+_E2M1_ROUNDING = (
+    (0.25, True, 0.0),
+    (0.75, False, 0.5),
+    (1.25, True, 1.0),
+    (1.75, False, 1.5),
+    (2.5, True, 2.0),
+    (3.5, False, 3.0),
+    (5.0, True, 4.0),
+)
+
+
+def _ref_round_to_e2m1(x):
+    magnitude = x.abs()
+    out = torch.full_like(magnitude, 6.0)
+    for bound, inclusive, value in reversed(_E2M1_ROUNDING):
+        below = magnitude <= bound if inclusive else magnitude < bound
+        out = torch.where(below, torch.full_like(out, value), out)
+    return out * torch.sign(x)
+
+
+def _ref_per_token_nvfp4_quantize(x):
+    """Pure-PyTorch per-token NVFP4 quantizer mirroring Transformer Engine's reference.
+
+    Returns E2M1 values ``[rows, cols]`` (FP32), E4M3 block decode scales
+    ``[rows, cols // 16]`` and the FP32 per-token decode scales ``[rows]``.
+    """
+    rows, cols = x.shape
+    blocks = x.float().view(rows, cols // 16, 16)
+    block_amax = blocks.abs().amax(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
+    row_amax = block_amax.amax(dim=1, keepdim=True)
+
+    # Tensor-by-tensor division: a Python scalar numerator becomes reciprocal-then-multiply.
+    def const(value):
+        return torch.tensor(value, dtype=torch.float32, device=x.device)
+
+    fp32_max = const(torch.finfo(torch.float32).max)
+    global_encode = torch.minimum(torch.div(const(448.0 * 6.0), row_amax), fp32_max)
+    global_encode = torch.where(global_encode == 0, torch.ones_like(global_encode), global_encode)
+    global_decode = torch.div(const(1.0), global_encode)
+    decode = torch.minimum(block_amax * (global_encode * torch.reciprocal(const(6.0))), fp32_max)
+    decode = decode.clamp(-448.0, 448.0).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+    encode = torch.minimum(torch.div(const(1.0), decode.float() * global_decode), fp32_max)
+    values = _ref_round_to_e2m1((blocks * encode).clamp(-6.0, 6.0)).reshape(rows, cols)
+    # An all-zero row reports a zero per-token scale.
+    per_token_decode = torch.where(row_amax == 0, torch.zeros_like(global_decode), global_decode)
+    return values, decode.squeeze(-1), per_token_decode.reshape(-1)
+
+
+def _unpack_e2m1(packed):
+    """Decode packed E2M1 bytes ``[rows, cols // 2]``; the low nibble is the even element."""
+    lookup = torch.tensor(_E2M1_VALUES, device=packed.device)
+    packed = packed.view(torch.uint8).long()
+    return torch.stack((lookup[packed & 0xF], lookup[packed >> 4]), dim=-1).flatten(-2)
+

+    quantizer reproduces, so it is the mode compared bit-exactly here.
+    """
+    from megatron.core.inference.moe.flashinfer_nvfp4 import quantize_routed_nvfp4_input

+    assert torch.equal(block_scale.view(torch.uint8), decode.view(torch.uint8))
+    assert torch.equal(_unpack_e2m1(data).reshape(tokens, hidden_size), values)

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("local_expert_offset", [0, 2, 4, 6])
+def test_flashinfer_routed_nvfp4_is_batch_invariant(local_expert_offset, mode, gated):
+    """A token's local-EP output must not depend on its batch or row position."""
+    from megatron.core.inference.moe.flashinfer_nvfp4 import (
+        flashinfer_routed_nvfp4_moe,
+        prepare_routed_nvfp4_weights,
+    )
+    from megatron.core.transformer.custom_layers.batch_invariant_kernels import (
+        set_batch_invariant_mode,
+    )
+
+    torch.manual_seed(1234)
+    num_experts, local_experts, hidden_size, intermediate_size = 8, 2, 512, 512
+    num_tokens, topk = 512, 2
+    local = slice(local_expert_offset, local_expert_offset + local_experts)
+    fc1_rows = 2 * intermediate_size if gated else intermediate_size
+    weights = prepare_routed_nvfp4_weights(
+        (torch.randn(num_experts, fc1_rows, hidden_size, device="cuda") * 0.05)[local]
+        .bfloat16()
+        .contiguous(),
+        (torch.randn(num_experts, hidden_size, intermediate_size, device="cuda") * 0.05)[local]
+        .bfloat16()
+        .contiguous(),
+    )
+    target = torch.randn(hidden_size, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    target_experts = torch.tensor([2, 5], device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
+    target_probs = torch.tensor([0.625, 0.375], device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32)
+
+    def _run(active_tokens: int, target_row: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+        # Neighbouring rows are 100x larger, which would dominate a tensor-wide scale,
+        # and share expert 2 with the target so its per-expert row count changes.
+        hidden = torch.randn(num_tokens, hidden_size, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16) * 100
+        routing_map = torch.full((num_tokens, topk), -1, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
+        routing_map[:active_tokens, 0] = 2
+        routing_map[:active_tokens, 1] = 3
+        probs = torch.rand(num_tokens, topk, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32)
+        probs[:active_tokens].fill_(0.5)
+        hidden[target_row].copy_(target)
+        routing_map[target_row].copy_(target_experts)
+        probs[target_row].copy_(target_probs)
+        return flashinfer_routed_nvfp4_moe(
+            hidden,
+            routing_map,
+            probs,
+            weights,
+            num_experts=num_experts,
+            local_expert_offset=local_expert_offset,
+            activation_type=_activation_type(gated),
+        )[target_row]
+
+    context = (
+        deterministic_algorithms(True)
+        if mode == "deterministic"
+        else set_batch_invariant_mode(True)
+    )
+    with torch.no_grad(), context:
+        output_alone = _run(1, 0)
+        output_batched = _run(128, 73)
+
+    assert torch.equal(output_alone, output_batched), (
+        "per-token NVFP4 output changed with the batch; max abs diff: "
+        f"{(output_alone.float() - output_batched.float()).abs().max().item()}"
+    )
+    if not any(local.start <= expert < local.stop for expert in target_experts.tolist()):
+        assert torch.count_nonzero(output_alone).item() == 0

+def test_flashinfer_routed_nvfp4_bounded_rows_match_full_buffer(gated):
+    """A bounded decode prefix gives the full buffer's rows and leaves the rest of out alone."""
+    from megatron.core.inference.moe.flashinfer_nvfp4 import (
+        flashinfer_routed_nvfp4_moe,
+        prepare_routed_nvfp4_weights,
+    )
+    from megatron.core.transformer.custom_layers.batch_invariant_kernels import (
+        set_batch_invariant_mode,
+    )
+
+    torch.manual_seed(1235)
+    num_experts, hidden_size, intermediate_size = 4, 512, 512
+    full_rows, capacity, active_tokens, topk = 512, 64, 40, 2
+    fc1_rows = 2 * intermediate_size if gated else intermediate_size
+    weights = prepare_routed_nvfp4_weights(
+        (torch.randn(num_experts, fc1_rows, hidden_size, device="cuda") * 0.05).bfloat16(),
+        (torch.randn(num_experts, hidden_size, intermediate_size, device="cuda") * 0.05).bfloat16(),
+    )
+    hidden = torch.randn(full_rows, hidden_size, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    # The dispatcher marks rows without a token -1, inside and past the prefix.
+    routing_map = torch.full((full_rows, topk), -1, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
+    routing_map[:active_tokens] = torch.randint(
+        num_experts, (active_tokens, topk), device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32
+    )
+    probs = torch.rand(full_rows, topk, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32)
+
+    def _run(**bounds):
+        out = torch.full((full_rows, hidden_size), 7.0, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+        flashinfer_routed_nvfp4_moe(
+            hidden,
+            routing_map,
+            probs,
+            weights,
+            num_experts=num_experts,
+            local_expert_offset=0,
+            activation_type=_activation_type(gated),
+            out=out,
+            **bounds,
+        )
+        return out
+
+    with torch.no_grad(), set_batch_invariant_mode(True):
+        full = _run()
+        bounded = _run(token_capacity=capacity, use_bounded_rows=True)
+        unbounded = _run(token_capacity=capacity, use_bounded_rows=False)
+
+    assert torch.equal(bounded[:capacity], full[:capacity])
+    assert torch.all(bounded[capacity:] == 7.0), "rows past the prefix were written"
+    assert torch.equal(unbounded, full), "use_bounded_rows=False must process the full buffer"

+def _dsa_golden_layer_terms(
+    args, total_tokens, seqlen_squared_sum, num_dsa_layers, num_indexer_layers
+):
+    """Golden DSA attention terms: ``(token_linear, core)`` coefficients.
+
+    Independent reimplementation of the per-DSA-layer absorbed-MLA projections,
+    top-k-scaled sparse core attention, and the indexer (with its own
+    KL-loss-dependent expansion). Multiply ``token_linear`` by the real token
+    count and ``core`` by ``sum(L^2)``. Shared by the standard-path golden
+    (``_dsa_golden_flops``) and the hybrid-path tests.
+    """
+    fwd_bwd = 3
+    fma = 2
+    nh = args.num_attention_heads
+
+    # ---- MLA projections (token-linear, per layer) ----
+    q_output_dim = nh * (args.qk_head_dim + args.qk_pos_emb_head_dim)
+    if args.q_lora_rank is None:
+        q_term = args.hidden_size * q_output_dim
+    else:
+        q_term = args.q_lora_rank * (args.hidden_size + q_output_dim + 1)
+    kv_term = (
+        args.kv_lora_rank * (args.hidden_size + nh * (args.qk_head_dim + args.v_head_dim) + 1)
+        + args.hidden_size * args.qk_pos_emb_head_dim
+    )
+    o_term = nh * args.v_head_dim * args.hidden_size
+    mla_proj_per_layer = fwd_bwd * fma * (q_term + kv_term + o_term)
+
+    # ---- Core attention: absorbed-MLA cost scaled down to top-k sparse pairs.
+    # DSA executes ``AbsorbedMLASelfAttention``: QK^T over the compressed KV
+    # latent (kv_lora_rank + rope per head) and AV over kv_lora_rank.
+    raw_core = nh * (args.kv_lora_rank + args.qk_pos_emb_head_dim) / 2 + nh * args.kv_lora_rank / 2
+    mean_seqlen = seqlen_squared_sum / total_tokens
+    topk = args.dsa_indexer_topk
+    if mean_seqlen <= topk:
+        sparse_scale = 1.0
+    else:
+        dense_pairs = mean_seqlen * mean_seqlen / 2
+        topk_pairs = topk * mean_seqlen - topk * topk / 2
+        sparse_scale = topk_pairs / dense_pairs
+    sparse_core_per_layer = fwd_bwd * fma * raw_core * sparse_scale
+
+    # ---- DSA indexer: only layers that compute their own top-k index ----
+    idx_dim = args.dsa_indexer_n_heads * args.dsa_indexer_head_dim
+    idx_token = num_indexer_layers * (
+        (args.hidden_size if args.q_lora_rank is None else args.q_lora_rank) * idx_dim  # wq_b
+        + args.hidden_size * args.dsa_indexer_head_dim  # wk
+        + args.hidden_size * args.dsa_indexer_n_heads  # weights_proj
+    )
+    idx_core = num_indexer_layers * idx_dim / 2
+    # The indexer only runs a backward pass when its KL loss is on, and its
+    # inputs are detached: projections pay fwd + wgrad, scoring pays fwd + dq + dk.
+    # Forward scoring is always dense; with the sparse KL loss the score
+    # gradient is nonzero only on the top-k pairs, so dq + dk shrink by the
+    # same top-k / dense pair ratio as core attention.
+    if (args.dsa_indexer_loss_coeff or 0.0) > 0:
+        idx_token_expansion = 2
+        if getattr(args, "dsa_indexer_use_sparse_loss", False):
+            idx_core_expansion = 1 + 2 * sparse_scale
+        else:
+            idx_core_expansion = 3
+    else:
+        idx_token_expansion, idx_core_expansion = 1, 1
+    dsa_extra_token = idx_token_expansion * fma * idx_token
+    dsa_extra_core = idx_core_expansion * fma * idx_core
+
+    self_attn_term = mla_proj_per_layer * num_dsa_layers + dsa_extra_token
+    self_attn_core_term = sparse_core_per_layer * num_dsa_layers + dsa_extra_core
+    return self_attn_term, self_attn_core_term
